text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- German trade union leader Schulte calls on unions to agree to new basic programme. He says DGB is going to stick together even though employers are expecting unions to damage themselves.
- Non-smokers should receive protection from passive smoke at workplace, according to new draft law proposed in parliament

- SPD says pension insurance system needs added funds injection from federal government, amount needs to be raised by 11 billion marks to 79 billon marks otherwise pension insurance rates will have to be raised.
- German economy being supported by exports, economic growth rises 1.2 percent in second quarter.
HANDELSBLATT
- EU says German government may sell Lufthansa, opening way for sale of government's last 35.68 percent stake.
- Veba will have another record earnings year, electricity division most profitable.

- Controversy over Telekom's decision to raise share offering to 600 million from 500 million. SPD wants Telekom to lower the share price towards 25 marks because of the expanded offering. The added shares will damp share price gains, SPD says.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- East German border guard chief Baumgarten arrested one day after supreme court rejects appeal against convictions of East German military leaders because of Berlin Wall shootings
- Defence Minister Ruehe wants to send 3,000 troops to Bosnia as part of IFOR.
- Grand coalition forming in parliament to protect rights of non-smokers.
DIE WELT
- DGB leader urges unions to work together, trade union conferences opens in Dresden, debate about basic program, IG Metall leader Zwickel threatens to leave early
- Parliamentarians propose legislation to forbid smoking at the work place
- SPD leader Gerhard Schroeder says he won't run as chancellor candidate in 1998 if SPD's chancellor candidate is selected by party primary again as in 1994.
- Proposed tax on investment profits controversial. economic advisory council warns against double taxation.
